proof_skeleton_nl: Fix a positive integer n, an integer j with 0 <= j <= n - 1, and a real x with j/n <= x < (j + 1)/n. Let d = x - j/n. By L1 and L2, we have 0 <= d < 1/n and x = J_{n,j}(d). By L4, K_{n,j}(d) <= K_{n,j}(0). By L3, this rewrites to F_n(x) <= F_n(j/n). Since n, j, and x were arbitrary subject to the hypotheses, this is exactly the theorem.

steps.derives: From j/n <= x < (j + 1)/n, obtain the offset coordinate d = x - j/n with 0 <= d < 1/n and x = J_{n,j}(d).
steps.trivial_justification: This combines the direct arithmetic offset calculation with the affine-coordinate description of the cell.

steps.derives: Apply the bottleneck inequality to the d from A1 to get K_{n,j}(d) <= K_{n,j}(0).
steps.trivial_justification: This is a direct instantiation of the local offset inequality at the chosen parameter d.

steps.derives: Rewrite K_{n,j}(d) as F_n(x) and K_{n,j}(0) as F_n(j/n), yielding F_n(x) <= F_n(j/n).
steps.trivial_justification: This step uses the definitional bridge from the offset coordinate back to the original function values.

steps.derives: Since n, j, and x were arbitrary under the hypotheses, conclude the universal theorem statement for all positive integers n, all integers j with 0 <= j <= n - 1, and all real x with j/n <= x < (j + 1)/n.
steps.trivial_justification: This is universal generalization from the fixed arbitrary variables in A3.
